examined_formations.title: EXISTING_MERCHANT_API_TO_TRANSACTIONAL_AGENT_SKILL_COMPILER
examined_formations.chinese_title: 已有商品/订单接口商家 → 可真实交易 Agent Skill 自动编译
examined_formations.evidence_summary: Alipay and WeChat now make agent payment/distribution real and explicitly leave merchant business logic to merchant Skills. Payment/distribution remain platform-owned, merchant Skill generation is already open-source, and OpenLuckin shows schema-driven real ordering over an official MCP.

attraction_brief.a_side: Merchants with existing digital catalogs/order endpoints want existing commerce callable from agents without rebuilding a consumer app.
attraction_brief.a_side_evidence: Alipay and WeChat publish merchant integration paths requiring merchant Skills while preserving merchant order/payment backends.
attraction_brief.b_side: Agents/users can execute merchant actions through Skill ecosystems and current AI-payment rails.
attraction_brief.b_side_evidence: WeChat SkillHub distributes merchant Skills; Alipay documents merchant order Skills handing payment to its payment Skill.
attraction_brief.operator: A compiler matters only if it repeatedly converts heterogeneous merchant APIs into safe production transaction Skills with little manual integration and owns a reusable acceptance/outcome asset.
attraction_brief.operator_non_labor_test: Must not require bespoke per-merchant semantic mapping, authentication surgery, order-state debugging and maintenance.
attraction_brief.connection_wow: Existing commerce becomes agent-callable once search/SKU/order semantics are exposed as a Skill and payment is delegated to native AI-pay rails.

exact_incumbent_and_control_surface_pref: WeChat owns SkillHub distribution and AI payment registration.
Open-source projects already generate merchant Skills/MCP services.
OpenLuckin generates an Agent-facing transaction flow around an official merchant MCP schema.

examined_formations.title: HOUSEKEEPING_CREDIT_AND_SERVICE_MATCH_ROUTER
examined_formations.chinese_title: 家政信用核验 → 服务匹配与下单路由
examined_formations.evidence_summary: Housekeeping trust and platform standardization are advancing, but the official credit mother platform is explicitly being embedded into order/dispatch/acceptance flows and standardized third-party integrations. The service remains physical human fulfillment.

attraction_brief.a_side: Households want trustworthy providers with verifiable identity, background, health and service information.
attraction_brief.a_side_evidence: MOFCOM embeds 家政信用查 query results into the consumer order flow.
attraction_brief.b_side: Housekeeping firms/workers want trusted demand and standardized digital onboarding.
attraction_brief.b_side_evidence: The official platform covers a large registered ecosystem and 2026 standards cover onboarding and platform quality.
attraction_brief.operator: A router needs a distinct trust or fulfillment control edge beyond the official query layer and existing platforms.
attraction_brief.operator_non_labor_test: Must not depend on recurring manual recruitment, schedule exceptions, disputes or household-service delivery.
attraction_brief.connection_wow: Trust verification can be pushed directly into the order flow.

examined_formations.title: AUTHORIZED_ECOMMERCE_AFTERSALES_ACTION_ROUTER
examined_formations.chinese_title: 商家授权电商售后状态 → 退款/审核动作路由
examined_formations.evidence_summary: Current e-commerce standards and platform APIs make after-sales state/action increasingly machine-readable and callable, but the rights are merchant/platform credentials and the difficult exception tail remains evidence/negotiation judgment.

attraction_brief.a_side: Merchants want lower after-sales handling cost and faster refund/dispute processing.
attraction_brief.a_side_evidence: Current platform APIs expose refund/after-sales state and merchant-authorized actions.
attraction_brief.b_side: Platforms/users want policy-compliant timely after-sales resolution.
attraction_brief.b_side_evidence: GB/Z 200-2026 formalizes after-sales service and platform flows expose structured refund operations.
attraction_brief.operator: A router matters only if cross-platform state plus outcomes produce a proprietary decision edge beyond merchant-owned credentials.
attraction_brief.operator_non_labor_test: Must not require humans to read evidence, negotiate or interpret bespoke policy on each exception.
attraction_brief.connection_wow: Structured after-sales events can trigger authorized refund/review actions instead of dashboard work.

examined_formations.title: NATURAL_LANGUAGE_CLOUD_OPERATIONS_GUARDRAIL_ROUTER
examined_formations.chinese_title: 自然语言云运维动作 → 权限/风险守卫路由
examined_formations.evidence_summary: Alibaba Cloud exposes broad OpenAPI actions to common agents through provider-native MCP with OAuth/static credentials, RAM controls, multi-account operation and orchestration. Action/control/audit remain provider/account owned.

attraction_brief.a_side: SMEs and operators want agents to execute cloud operations without hand-writing every OpenAPI call.
attraction_brief.a_side_evidence: Alibaba Cloud Core MCP supports natural-language API matching/calling, multi-step orchestration and common AI clients.
attraction_brief.b_side: Cloud control planes expose actions under customer account credentials and RAM policy.
attraction_brief.b_side_evidence: Official docs support OAuth/static credentials, RAM permissions and multi-account assumed-role access.
attraction_brief.operator: A guardrail needs an operator-owned policy/outcome advantage beyond provider permissions and generic agent approvals.
attraction_brief.operator_non_labor_test: Must not become recurring human cloud review, bespoke runbook authoring or managed operations.
attraction_brief.connection_wow: Natural-language agents can call a broad cloud control plane directly through provider-native MCP.

excluded_observations: Generic merchant-Skill creation was excluded because public generators already cover merchant facts/services.
Agent payment itself was excluded because payment callability is provider-owned enabling infrastructure.
Housekeeping standards were not treated as proof that an independent marketplace owns supply or service-quality control.
